newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai stocks plunge following HK handover.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai stocks plunge following HK handover.

text.p: Shanghai's foreign currency B shares and domestic currency A shares plunged on Wednesday on the first day of trading after the return of Hong Kong to Chinese rule due to poor market sentiment, brokers said.
The British colony of Hong Kong returned to Chinese sovereignty at midnight on Monday.
The B index fell 2.788 points or 3.42 percent to end the day at 78.690 points on volume of 8.610 million shares worth $5.040 million.
"The fading of euphoria over the return of Hong Kong together with sharp falls in the A share index dragged down the B shares today," said a broker at a major local securities firm.
The A index plunged 53.764 points or 4.11 percent to 1,253.014 points on volume of 372.868 million shares worth 5.608 billion yuan.
The fall was not caused by negative sentiment towards the future of Hong Kong, but rather the realization the passing of the event will no longer help boost the market, brokers said.
"Investors cannot find a new excuse to support the market, so institutions were seen cashing in their chips for profit," said the local securities firm broker.
"Technical charts also showed the B index could fall further in the short term due to heavy selling pressure," he said.

The Hong Kong handover boosted sentiment earlier this year but buying support was absent on Wednesday as investors looked towards the future and sold on expectations of a flood of new issues which are aimed at cooling the markets, brokers said.

Investors are now also looking towards the reporting of 1997 interim results by listed-companies in July and August, as well as any signs of government credit easing before returning to the market to buy, they said.
Of 45 B shares, 41 traded with 27 down, seven flat and seven up.
Shanghai Vacuum And Electron Device Co was the biggest loser on selling due to expectations of poor results. It fell $0.020 or 10.00 percent to $0.180.
Recently-listed Hainan Airlines Co was the most actively traded B share on profit-taking, falling $0.010 or 1.83 percent to $0.536 on volume of around 1.8 million shares.
Shanghai Shuanglu Electric Appliance Co was the biggest A share loser on expectations of poor results, plunging 0.79 yuan or 10.03 percent to 7.09 yuan.
The SSE30 blue chip index ended down 117.188 points or 2.88 percent to 3,949.330 points.
Brokers said both A and B shares could fall further later this week as market sentiment will continue to be hurt by expectations of negative news.
